an0827.user: Post-iOS my dashboards are a mess and I can't tell what's real. Meta says my WhatsApp + Meta campaigns are pulling 4.4 ROAS. Shopify, on last-click, says 1.6 on the same ₹19L spend. That's a massive gap. Which dashboard do I actually trust?
an0827.assistant: Neither, and that's the honest answer — you're refereeing two scorekeepers who will never agree because they're both biased in opposite directions. Meta's 4.4 is modelled: it counts 7-day-click, claims view-through conversions, and gives itself credit for sales it merely influenced — so it flatters. Shopify last-click at 1.6 hands all the credit to whatever the customer touched last (a Google search of your brand, a direct visit) and gives Meta nothing for the demand it created up-funnel — so it undercounts. The truth sits somewhere between 1.6 and 4.4, and no amount of staring will reconcile them post-iOS. So stop trying to pick a winner between the dashboards. Anchor on a number neither platform can spin: blended CAC = total spend ÷ actual new customers. Take your ₹19L, divide by the count of genuinely new customers Shopify recorded that period, and manage to that single figure month over month. If blended CAC is falling and contribution per customer covers it, you're winning regardless of what either ROAS claims. Caveat: 'new' has to mean new — strip repeat buyers out of that denominator or you'll flatter yourself the same way Meta does.
